items.item_text: Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Doctorate of Pharmacy degree or equivalent clinical experience.
Five (5) years of clinical pharmacist experience (not including residency).
Strong knowledge and experience in medication use processes, including experience with medication infusion administration.
Postgraduate residency training highly desired (PGY1 experience or equivalent clinical experience), PGY2 highly preferred.
Clinical pharmacist experience in the inpatient setting highly desired.
Medication-use evaluation experience.
The Medication Safety and Delivery Pharmacist position will be responsible for the following:
Build and maintain medication delivery pump libraries
Work with the department Medication Safety Pharmacists on Medication Error Reduction Plan (MERP) initiatives
Attend and participate in monthly Safe Medication Practices (SMP) sub-committee meetings
Attend and participate in MERP subcommittee meetings when pump expertise needed
Attend and participate in committee, pharmacy, and/or nurse staff meetings to provide pump education or when expertise needed
Facilitate review and solution generation for infusion/medication pump related iReports
Facilitate review and solution generation for quality metrics related to medication pumps/medication administration
Additional roles may include but are not limited to:
Interpret, update, and manage pharmacy department and health system policies as related to medication safety delivery
Directly observes and analyses the medication use process
Precept pharmacy students, PGY1 pharmacy residents, and PGY2 pharmacy residents
The Medication Safety and Delivery Pharmacist will spend 40% of their time in medication use/operational activities.
Registered Pharmacist - issued by the state of California (RPH).
Documented record of improvement in and contributions to the respective area of specialty practice through CQI projects, participation in nursing in-services, protocol development, etc.
Ongoing appointments to appropriate drug policy and other committees of the organization.
Serving regularly as a reviewer of contributed papers or manuscripts submitted for publication on topics related to the specialty practice.
Demonstrated a commitment to teaching (e.g. through preceptorship, education of medical center staff through clinical forums, grand rounds, etc.)
Proven leadership in advancing the profession of pharmacy through active service in professional organizations at the local, state, and national levels.
Demonstrated ability to lead committees, workgroups, projects, or interdisciplinary teams.

A sustained record of contributing to the total body of knowledge in the specialty area of pharmacy practice annually through (1) research, (2) publications in professional journals, and/or (3) presentations at professional meetings.
